Не переводите каждую форму механически к: Do not translate the forms mechanically. English normally requires a present-tense form of “be”: Diák vagyok means “I am a student.” Hungarian differs especially in the third person: van/vannak are omitted with professions, nationalities, and qualities, but kept for location and existence.
Не переносите русские слова в венгерское: Do not build a Hungarian sentence by inserting English words or translating word for word. In the third person, do not add van with a profession or nationality. Check the exact forms vagyok, vagy, van, vagyunk, vagytok, vannak.
Не путайте ti и вежливое «Вы». Ti означа: Do not confuse ti with formal address. Ti is informal plural “you”. Hungarian uses Ön for formal address to one person and Önök for formal address to several people. English “you” covers all of these, so pay attention to both number and formality.
Do not confuse vowel length with stress.
Do not confuse stress with vowel length. The marks in á, é, í, ó, ő, ú, and ű indicate vowel length, not stress.
Не пытайтесь угадывать произношение по р: Do not guess Hungarian pronunciation from an English-style respelling. Use the Hungarian audio as the model. The English translation gives the meaning, not the sound of the word.
Не смешивайте три разных значения:: Do not mix up these three meanings:
Не сокращайте правила до формул «вопрос: Do not reduce the rules to “question = intonation” and “negation = nem”. Intonation without a question word applies mainly to yes/no questions, while negative location/existence sentences with van/vannak use nincs/nincsenek.
Не ставьте nem механически перед любой ф: Don’t put nem mechanically before any form of “be.” In neutral sentences, the negations of van and vannak are the special forms nincs and nincsenek.
Не читайте слова по русским буквам. Снач: Do not read Hungarian words through English spelling habits. Listen to the Hungarian model first, then repeat. Any written pronunciation guide is only approximate.

Округлите губы как для «у», язык держите: Round your lips as for /u/ while keeping the tongue in the /i/ position. Hungarian ü is /y/ and has no native English equivalent.
